title: Psalms Chapter 96 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 96 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 96 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 96.

questions.question: What are the people instructed to do in Psalms 96?
options: Sing unto the LORD a new song
questions.correctAnswer: Sing unto the LORD a new song
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with the command to sing unto the LORD a new song in Psalms 96:1.

questions.question: Which name is to be blessed according to Psalms 96:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:2 instructs to sing unto the LORD and bless His name.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:3, what should be declared among the heathen?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:3 encourages declaring the glory of the LORD and His wonders among all people.

questions.question: What is said about the LORD in Psalms 96:4?
options: He is to be feared above all gods
He is the creator of all
He is the strongest of all
He is the wisest of all
questions.correctAnswer: He is to be feared above all gods
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:4 states that the LORD is great and greatly to be praised and is to be feared above all gods.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:5, what are all the gods of the nations described as?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:5 declares that all the gods of the nations are idols, contrasting them with the LORD who made the heavens.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96 instructs to show forth the LORD's salvation from day to day.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:2 specifically states to show forth His salvation from day to day.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96:6 mentions that strength and beauty are in the LORD's sanctuary.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:6 says that honour and majesty are before Him, and strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.

questions.question: What should be done in the beauty of holiness according to Psalms 96:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:9 instructs to worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:10, what should be said among the heathen?
options: The earth is full of wickedness
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:10 commands to say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96 states that the world will be established and shall not be moved.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:10 mentions that the world shall be established that it shall not be moved.

questions.question: In what way should the heavens and earth respond according to Psalms 96:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:11 calls for the heavens to rejoice and the earth to be glad.

questions.question: In Psalms 96, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: The very first instruction in Psalms 96:1 is to sing unto the LORD a new song.

questions.question: What is said about the trees of the wood in Psalms 96:12?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:12 states that all the trees of the wood shall rejoice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:13, what does the LORD come to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:13 declares that the LORD comes to judge the earth.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96:4 says the LORD is to be feared above all gods.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:4 clearly states that the LORD is to be feared above all gods.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 96 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 96 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is said to be before the LORD in Psalms 96:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:6 states, 'Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.' This highlights the attributes associated with the presence of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:8, what should we bring into the LORD's courts?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:8 instructs, 'Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.' This emphasizes the importance of honoring God with our gifts.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96:10 states that the world shall be moved.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:10 states, 'the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved,' indicating stability rather than movement.

questions.question: What should the kindreds of the people give unto the LORD according to Psalms 96:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:7 says, 'Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people, give unto the LORD glory and strength,' emphasizing the call to recognize God's power.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:9, how should we worship the LORD?
options: In the joy of our hearts
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:9 states, 'O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness,' indicating that worship should be done with reverence and purity.

questions.question: True or False: The gods of the nations are depicted as real in Psalms 96:5.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:5 declares, 'For all the gods of the nations are idols,' indicating that they are not real and do not compare to the LORD.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:11 encourage the heavens and the earth to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:11 says, 'Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad,' encouraging all of creation to celebrate God's reign.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:10 reveal about the LORD's judgment?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:10 concludes, 'he shall judge the people righteously,' indicating that God's judgment is fair and just.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:3 instruct us to declare among the heathen?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:3 instructs, 'Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all people,' emphasizing the importance of sharing God's greatness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:12, what will happen to the trees of the wood?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:12 states, 'then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice,' indicating creation's response to God's coming judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 96:2 teach us about the importance of daily faith?
options: It emphasizes the need for constant prayer
It highlights the need for daily blessings
It calls for daily proclamation of salvation
It suggests weekly worship is enough
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for daily proclamation of salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:2 states, 'shew forth his salvation from day to day,' emphasizing the importance of sharing God's salvation consistently.

questions.question: True or False: The passage encourages us to fear the LORD according to Psalms 96:9.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:9 says, 'fear before him, all the earth,' indicating that a healthy fear of the LORD is encouraged as part of worship.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 96 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 96.

questions.question: What is to be declared among the heathen according to Psalms 96?
questions.explanation: The verse states to 'Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all people.' (Psalms 96:3)

questions.question: Which of the following attributes is NOT mentioned in relation to the Lord in Psalms 96?
questions.explanation: The attributes mentioned in the chapter include greatness, fearfulness, honor, majesty, strength, and beauty, but wisdom is not listed (Psalms 96:4-6).

questions.question: According to Psalms 96, how should the earth respond to the Lord's coming?
questions.explanation: The text encourages the heavens to rejoice and the earth to be glad (Psalms 96:11).

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:13 say the Lord will do?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that the Lord 'cometh to judge the earth' (Psalms 96:13).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 96 states that all gods of the nations are real and powerful.
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:5 declares that 'For all the gods of the nations are idols,' indicating they are not real or powerful.

questions.question: What offering is mentioned in Psalms 96 that should be brought to the Lord?
questions.explanation: The chapter instructs to 'Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.' (Psalms 96:8)

questions.question: According to Psalms 96, what should be the attitude of the earth when the Lord comes?
questions.explanation: The chapter encourages a joyful response from the earth and its inhabitants, as stated in Psalms 96:12.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord is described as being to be feared above all gods in Psalms 96.
questions.explanation: The text affirms that 'he is to be feared above all gods.' (Psalms 96:4)

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the Lord's reign?
questions.explanation: Revelation 11:15 states, 'The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord,' echoing the theme of God's reign as mentioned in Psalms 96:10.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Psalms 96:11-12 when referring to the creation's response?
questions.explanation: The verses use personification as they attribute joy and rejoicing to the heavens, earth, and trees (Psalms 96:11-12).

questions.question: What Hebrew word for beauty in Psalms 96 may signify both external and internal qualities?
questions.explanation: The word 'Hadrah' in Psalms 96:6 signifies beauty, which can encompass both external and internal qualities, reflecting the glory of God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 96 connect with Psalms 145 regarding the theme of God's greatness?
options: Both proclaim His greatness and works
questions.correctAnswer: Both proclaim His greatness and works
questions.explanation: Both Psalms emphasize God's greatness and His wonderful works, as seen in Psalms 96:4 and Psalms 145:3.

questions.question: What is the main theme of Psalms 96 that connects to the prophetic anticipation in Isaiah?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96 anticipates a time when all nations will praise the Lord, a theme echoed in Isaiah's prophecies about the nations coming to worship (Isaiah 66:23).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 96 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 96 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What new action does Psalms 96:1 encourage all the earth to take?
options: To sing a new song to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To sing a new song to the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:1 calls for all the earth to sing unto the LORD a new song, emphasizing the joy and freshness of worship.

questions.question: In Psalms 96:3, what are believers instructed to declare among the nations?
questions.explanation: The verse directs believers to declare the LORD's glory and wonders among the heathen, highlighting God's greatness to all people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:4, how is the LORD described in relation to other gods?
options: He is to be feared above all gods
He is equal to all gods
He is indifferent to other gods
questions.correctAnswer: He is to be feared above all gods
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:4 states that the LORD is great and greatly to be praised, signifying His superiority over all other gods.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:5 say about the gods of the nations?
questions.explanation: The verse asserts that all the gods of the nations are idols, contrasting them with the living God who made the heavens.

questions.question: What attributes of God are highlighted in Psalms 96:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:6 speaks of honour and majesty being before the LORD, showcasing His divine attributes.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:7, what should the kindreds of the people give to the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs kindreds to give unto the LORD glory and strength, recognizing His greatness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:8 instruct regarding offerings?
options: To bring an offering and come into His courts
questions.correctAnswer: To bring an offering and come into His courts
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving the glory due to His name and bringing offerings to the LORD.

questions.question: In the beauty of what should worship be conducted according to Psalms 96:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:9 calls for worship in the beauty of holiness, underscoring the sacredness of worship.

questions.question: What proclamation does Psalms 96:10 encourage to be made among the heathen?
questions.explanation: This verse encourages declaring that the LORD reigns, affirming His sovereignty and justice.

questions.question: What joyous reaction is called for in Psalms 96:11?
options: The heavens rejoice and the earth be glad
questions.correctAnswer: The heavens rejoice and the earth be glad
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:11 calls for rejoicing in the heavens and gladness in the earth, celebrating God's reign.

questions.question: What will happen to the trees of the wood according to Psalms 96:12?
questions.explanation: Psalms 96:12 states that all the trees of the wood will rejoice, reflecting creation's joy in God's coming judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 96:13, how will the LORD judge the world?
questions.explanation: The verse declares that the LORD will judge the world with righteousness, emphasizing His just nature.

questions.question: What combined message do Psalms 96:3 and 96:10 convey about the nature of God?
questions.explanation: Both verses instruct declaring God’s glory and proclaiming His reign, highlighting His majesty and authority.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is expressed in the combination of Psalms 96:4 and 96:5?
options: God's greatness and the folly of idols
questions.correctAnswer: God's greatness and the folly of idols
questions.explanation: These verses contrast the greatness of the LORD with the fact that the gods of the nations are mere idols.

questions.question: What does Psalms 96:1-2 reveal about the nature of worship in relation to salvation?
options: It should be joyful and continuous
questions.correctAnswer: It should be joyful and continuous
questions.explanation: The verses encourage singing a new song and blessing the LORD daily, showing that worship is ongoing and filled with joy.
